name: study-4-growth-division
title: Study 4 — growth & division: one individual becomes a heterogeneous population
objective:
The precarious individual grows as its autopoietic loop runs and, past a size
threshold, DIVIDES into two daughters. The membrane is partitioned with noise so
daughters differ in size; a heritable trait is inherited with mutation so lineages
DIVERSIFY over generations — one individual becomes a population of non-identical
individuals. Division is itself precarious: a daughter that inherits too little
membrane to maintain itself dissolves — reproduction has a viability cost. This
heterogeneous population is the substrate on which study 5's selection can act.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
A founder reproduces into a population whose individuals differ in composition,
and division carries a viability cost (some daughters dissolve).

behavior_tests.name: reproduction
behavior_tests.description:
The precarious identity is inherited: a single founder grows and divides into a
population — the closed, self-maintaining individual reproduces across generations.

behavior_tests.name: heterogeneity
behavior_tests.description:
The population is diverse: noisy partitioning at division and heritable mutation
diversify lineages, so individuals differ measurably in composition (trait spread > 0).

provenance.note: Existence-level band (this is an exploratory study): the threshold asks only whether trait diversity emerges at all (spread > ~0), not a calibrated or literature-anchored magnitude.

behavior_tests.name: division-precariousness
behavior_tests.description:
Reproduction has a viability cost: a daughter that inherits too little membrane to
maintain itself dissolves. Division is precarious — not every daughter survives.

provenance.note: Existence-level band: any non-zero daughter mortality demonstrates reproduction carries a viability cost. Exploratory threshold (does the cost occur at all?), not a calibrated rate.

findings.statement: The precarious identity is inherited: one founder grows and divides into a population of 300, and noisy partitioning + heritable mutation diversify the lineages (trait spread 0.11). One individual becomes a population of non-identical individuals.
Reproduction is precarious: 10% of daughters inherit too little membrane to maintain themselves and dissolve. Division has a viability cost — the same self-maintenance, now across generations.

resolved_uncertainties: One founder grows and divides into a heterogeneous population (robust across 12 seeds; reaches carrying every seed).
Division is precarious: daughters that inherit too little membrane dissolve.
remaining_uncertainties: Reproduction is ENGINEERED — explicit division, inheritance and partitioning rules — not shown to EMERGE from autopoietic self-maintenance (review C7).
No control distinguishing engineered copying from autopoietic self-reproduction.

alternate_hypotheses.hypothesis: The population growth demonstrates engineered copying, not autopoietic self-reproduction.
alternate_hypotheses.why_plausible: the split/inherit/partition rules are coded, not derived from the membrane/metabolism loop.
discriminating_observables: a no-self-maintenance reproduction control: copies that do not metabolise should still 'divide' but not persist
coupling of division rate to self-production rate

followup_study_proposals.title: Engineered vs autopoietic reproduction (negative control)
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Show the metric must couple reproduction to self-maintenance — copying without metabolism should not qualify (review C7).

controls.name: self-maintaining-lineage
controls.hypothesis: A lineage that self-maintains should grow to carrying.

controls.name: no-self-maintenance-reproduction
controls.hypothesis: Reproduction without self-maintenance (no supply) should COLLAPSE — engineered copying alone is not autopoietic.

falsifiability: The 'reproduction extends autopoiesis' reading would be unsupported if the no-self-maintenance control still reached carrying — i.e. if engineered division persisted without metabolism.

alternative_hypotheses.claim: The population growth demonstrates engineered copying, not autopoietic self-reproduction.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminated_by: the no-self-maintenance negative control (supply=0) collapses despite division firing, so persistence requires self-maintenance.

derived.insight: The precarious identity is inherited: one founder grows and divides into a population of 300, and noisy partitioning + heritable mutation diversify the lineages (trait spread 0.11). One individual becomes a population of non-identical individuals.
